conviction_note: Near-non-result. Q3 cat losses were light industry-wide (+), but commercial middle-market underlying loss ratios worsened at peers (Hartford M&L, Chubb NA commercial) and the Orlando hotel market weakened (Comcast theme parks EBITDA -17%). The negatives are proxies or small segments on a name with a 0.96% median reaction. impact_sum -0.40 and scaled -0.07 agree in sign; scaled is smaller because p_up sits at 48 (proxies plus the known pessimism artefact) and nothing decides this print.
bar: There is no sourced Loews consensus: one aggregator shows a single-analyst FY2026 EPS of $8.25 and nothing for the quarter (https://intrinsicalpha.com/equity/nyse/l/estimates). The working bar is CNA's Q3 2026 core EPS. Chartmill puts it at $1.23 (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/CNA/estimates); Benzinga has $1.19 and Zacks cut to $1.19 in August (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CNA/earnings-forecasts). Q2 2026 actual was $1.19 and Q3 2025 was $1.50. The two sources disagree slightly and the bar is not Loews's own, so every finding is capped small.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 was a benign catastrophe quarter by the industry's own counts. Gallagher Re puts 9M26 global insured cat losses at $92bn, the lowest since 2019, with no single event over $10bn and a slow Atlantic season. Hurricane Isaias landed 9 Oct, outside Q3. CNA's Q2 2026 had $60M of pretax cats (2.3 pts) and the CNA bar ($1.19-1.23) is roughly a repeat of Q2's $1.19, so a light Q3 cat load leans toward meeting or beating that bar. Against Q3 2025's very low $41M, though, peers' cats rose year on year (Travelers $538M vs $302M; W.R. Berkley ~$86M vs ~$79M), mainly from severe convective storms.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Loews has not traded on CNA cat lines: Q3 2025 (CNA core record $1.50, cats $41M) moved -0.14% on 2025-11-03; Q2 2026 moved +0.21% (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: The CNA bar has sat at $1.19-1.23 since a Zacks cut in mid-August and was not raised after the benign-quarter data. If the light cat quarter were priced, CNA estimates would have moved up after Gallagher's 21 Oct report and Travelers' 16 Oct print; no revision was found. The effect is still small, because cats are a minor line for CNA.
findings.independence: Travelers Q3 2026 8-K: cats $538M, mostly wind/hail, combined ratio 86.8% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000086312/000008631226000180/a991pressrelease93026.htm). W.R. Berkley Q3 cats ~$85.9M vs ~$78.5M (https://www.insurancejournal.com/news/national/2026/10/20/889600.htm). Both are proxies, not CNA's own number.

findings.finding: Commercial middle-market loss trends worsened at peers in Q3 2026, and that is CNA's core book. Hartford's Middle & Large Business underlying combined ratio was 99.5, against 91.4 a year earlier and 95.3 in Q2 2026, on workers' comp and non-cat property; the trade press reported it on 2026-10-27 as a trend, not a one-off. Chubb's North America commercial combined ratio worsened to 86.3 from 81.5, with $13M of unfavorable long-tail development. CNA already raised its 2026 underlying loss picks in Q2 (underlying combined ratio 94.2 vs 91.7), so further deterioration would come on top of that.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Loews's largest move in the baseline, -5.86% on 2026-05-04, came when CNA's combined ratio rose to 102.2% on a $106M reserve charge plus a 2.6-pt underlying loss-ratio increase (https://rallies.ai/news/loews-drops-after-q1-profit-declines-as-cna-reserve-charge-hits-underwriting-results). Q2 2026 brought a 2.5-pt underlying increase with no PYD, and the stock moved +0.21%.
findings.why_not_priced: Hartford spoke on 26-27 Oct, after CNA and Loews last spoke (3 Aug), and the CNA bar ($1.19-1.23) was set before that. If the market had priced it, CNA estimates would have been trimmed in late October, or Loews would have lagged the insurance group in the last week; Loews is flat over 5 days (-0.16%). The read-across is weakened by two peers: Selective booked zero casualty PYD and Chubb's long-tail adverse was only $13M.
findings.independence: Chubb Q3 2026: NA commercial combined ratio 86.3 vs 81.5, long-tail unfavorable $13M (https://www.reinsurancene.ws/chubb-posts-record-5-79bn-pc-underwriting-income-for-first-nine-months-of-2026/). Against it, Selective had zero prior-year casualty development in Q3 2026 (https://actuary.info/insights/selective-q3-2026-zero-prior-year-casualty-development-cat-losses-5-4-points-npw-down-7-percent) and Hartford's overall PYD was favorable at $61M. Proxy only; CNA has not confirmed.

findings.finding: Q3 is when CNA books its annual Life & Group reserve review, a one-off inside the print. The last two were small: Q3 2025 LTC assumption update +$7M pretax to reserves (about $7M after-tax hit to core per the release), and Q3 2024 +$15M pretax. CNA also did a $1bn LTC portfolio trade in Q2 2026 that extended duration. Nothing points to a large Q3 2026 update, but this is the one scheduled reserve event in the quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 (LTC update ~$7M) moved -0.14%; Q3 2024's update was $15M pretax. Neither shows a reaction attributable to the review.
findings.why_not_priced: It is unquantified until the release. If the market expected a large LTC charge, CNA estimates would sit below the $1.19 Q2 run-rate rather than at or above it. The size is near zero because the history is small; the range carries the tail.
findings.independence: The CNA Q3 2025 10-Q gives the same $7M pretax update and Q3 2024 at $15M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/21175/000002117525000097/cna-20250930.htm), so it shares a source family. The Loews Q2 2026 earnings remarks describe the $1bn LTC portfolio trade (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000060086/000006008626000045/exhibit992-q22026.htm).

findings.finding: Loews Hotels faces a weaker Q3 at its biggest market. Comcast reported on 2026-10-22 that Theme Parks Q3 2026 revenue fell 4.4% to $2,597M and Adjusted EBITDA fell 17.1% to $780M, on lower admissions and more promotions, and said Orlando softness would continue into Q4 and 1H27. Loews Hotels' Universal Orlando JV hotels drove its Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA up 26% to $137M. The Q3 2025 comparison is $69M Adjusted EBITDA (+8%), and the three new Orlando hotels are no longer an incremental year-on-year driver. Net of the rest of the company: hotels are about $69M of EBITDA in a quarter where CNA plus Boardwalk earn about $400M after tax to Loews, so even a 20% hotel miss is roughly $0.05 a share.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Hotels have never been the reaction line. Q1 2026 hotels Adjusted EBITDA +53% came with a -5.86% move driven by CNA; Q2 2026 hotels +26% came with +0.21%.
findings.why_not_priced: Comcast is a counterparty that spoke after Loews last did (3 Aug), and Loews has almost no sell-side coverage to carry the read-across. In the Q2 remarks Loews said there was 'still ramp ahead' and made no mention of softness. The finding stays small because the segment is small.
findings.independence: Comcast's Q2 2026 call said Orlando attendance softened from June and stayed pressured into Q3 (https://blogmickey.com/2026/07/universal-confirms-orlando-tourism-summer-softness-attendance-below-expectations/, 2026-07-23). That is the same company, so it is not fully independent. Loews Q3 2025 hotels base of $69M: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/60086/000006008625000177/exhibit991-q32025.htm.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 equity returns were weak outside mega-caps: S&P 500 total return +2.3% but equal-weight -1.87% (Morgan Stanley), against a very strong Q3 2025. That leans against CNA's limited-partnership and common-stock income, which was $131M in Q2 2026 and $71M in Q3 2025, and against the parent's trading portfolio. Loews's Q3 2025 corporate segment earned $42M, already down on lower trading income, and the parent's trading fixed maturities shrank to $291M at 2026-06-30 from $633M at year end, so the parent leg is smaller now.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Investment-income swings have not been isolated as a reaction line. Q3 2025 (record CNA core, corporate down) moved -0.14%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is macro-to-company inference. CNA's LP accounting may run on a lag, and the cap-weighted index was positive. It is small and unconfirmed by the company.
findings.independence: First Trust gives a Q3 2026 S&P 500 total return of 2.3% (https://www.ftportfolios.com/Commentary/EconomicResearch/2026/10/22/sp-500-index-through-q3-2026). The trading-portfolio size comes from the Loews Q2 2026 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000060086/000006008626000047/l-20260630.htm). Proxy.

findings.finding: Loews's buyback pace has been slow in 2026: $179M for 1H26, of which $146M (1.4M shares) came in Q2. Shares outstanding were 204,427,720 on 2026-07-31, essentially unchanged from 30 June, so little or nothing was repurchased in July. The parent held $4.4bn of cash and investments against $1.8bn of debt. The Q3 share count in the release will show whether repurchases resumed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Buyback figures are disclosed every quarter and have never moved the stock measurably. Q2 2026's $146M came with +0.21%.
findings.why_not_priced: The pace is already public in the 10-Q cover share count, so this is likely priced. It is filed for completeness and sized at zero.
findings.independence: The Q2 2026 earnings remarks give 1.7M shares and $179M since year end, with no post-quarter figure (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000060086/000006008626000045/exhibit992-q22026.htm). Same source family.

outside_window.finding: Hurricane Isaias landed in the Florida Panhandle on 9 Oct 2026 as a Category 2 storm, with industry insured losses estimated in the low-to-mid single-digit billions. It is a Q4 cat item for CNA and could only appear as commentary in this print; the reported Q4 number comes in early 2027.

Rule 5 (proxies smaller): cat-quarter proxy +0.2 -> +0.15 and Hartford/Chubb middle-market read-across -0.3 -> -0.25
Rule 2 (one-offs as one-offs): LTC annual review -0.1 -> -0.05, refiled as one_off
Rule 9 (net of the rest of the company): hotels finding -0.2 -> -0.15, with the net-of-rest arithmetic written in
Pessimism artefact: p_up 47 -> 48, so the scaled number moved from -0.11 to -0.07
Rule 7: short interest checked before the negatives (2.2% of shares, 3.8 days to cover); not crowded, so no further cut
Rule 8: no confirmed unpriced company-level number, so abs_move_pct was not raised further
